items.text: `cleanDoubleSlashes` in ufo takes an opt-in second parameter `respectQueryAndFragment` (same name as on the trailing-slash helpers), decided 2026-11-04. When `true`, only the part before the first `?` or `#` is cleaned, so `/foo//bar?redirect=//baz` becomes `/foo/bar?redirect=//baz`. Default behaviour is unchanged and still collapses `//` in the query and fragment, which had been corrupting redirect targets. Tests in `test/double-slash.test.ts` cover query only, fragment only, both, `?` inside a fragment, protocol URLs, inputs starting with `?` or `#`, empty input, and default/`false` still collapsing the query. The full suite passed (499 tests) and prettier was clean; the changes were uncommitted on branch `fix/double-slashes`.

Query handling in ufo evolved through releases: 1.0.0 removed undefined from withQuery (#71); 1.0.1 made QueryValue array-only like QueryObject values (#101) and handled empty array values uniformly (#103); v1.1.0 stringifies query values (#123) and encodes `[]`/`{}` in values (#118); v1.2.0 added generic types for getQuery/parseQuery (#131), made parsed query types string only (#139), had stringifyQuery filter empty values (#148), and parseQuery decode spaces in keys (#150); v1.6.0/v1.6.1 (April 2025) added `filterQuery` (#287) and made `parseQuery` return a null-prototype object via `Object.create(null)` (#286, #290) to avoid prototype issues.

Other ufo URL utility additions and fixes across releases: windows file URL leading-slash fix (1.0.0, #87); parseHost fix for hostnames with/without port (v1.1.0, #120, port kept as a string after a revert); `parseFilename` utility (#125) and joinURL leading-dot handling (#35) in v1.2.0; in v1.5.4 (July 2024) `parseURL` only normalizes Windows drive letters with `file://` (#246) and `withProtocol` considers relative protocol (#242); in v1.6.0/v1.6.1 `parseFilename` uses optional chaining for `opts.strict` (#284).

Query handling changed in v1.6.0/v1.6.1: `filterQuery` was added (#287), and `parseQuery` now uses a null-prototype object (#286, #290 with `Object.create(null)`). `parseFilename` uses optional chaining for `opts.strict` (#284). | When: 2025-04-07 to 2025-04-08 | Involving: Kricsleo, Pooya Parsa, Ezra Ashenafi | Null-prototype objects avoid prototype issues in parsed queries

ufo URL joining evolved in 2024: `joinURL` handles `../` segments (#217, rewritten in #218) and `joinRelativeURL` was added (#220) in v1.5.0. Follow-ups: base with protocol (#222, v1.5.1); a lookbehind regex was limited to `joinRelativeURL` (#226, v1.5.2) and then removed for browser compatibility (#228, v1.5.3).

URL protocol detection in ufo has been progressively hardened: parseURL handles `data:` and `blob` protocols (#159), ignores leading whitespace in parseURL/hasProtocol/isScriptProtocol (#170), parses protocols case-insensitively (#188), and script protocols are tested case-insensitively (#180); `stringifyParsedURL` supports partial inputs (#166). Shipped in v1.3.0 (2023-08-24) and v1.3.1 (2023-09-28). Earlier, hasProtocol gained strict mode (#124) and backslash acceptance (#122) in v1.1.0, no longer treated a windows drive letter as a protocol in 1.0.1 (#106), and `isScriptProtocol` was added in v1.2.0 (#156).

URL joining enhancements: `joinURL` handles `../` segments (#217, rewritten in #218), and new `joinRelativeURL` was added (#220) in v1.5.0.
